parts.visual:
A technical founder built the MVP in their bedroom. Now the company has 30 engineers. The founder still reviews every single line of code before it gets deployed. The engineering team is paralyzed because the founder is the ultimate bottleneck.

The Evolution:
1. The Transition: To grow from $1M to $10M, the founder must transition from 'Maker' (writing code) to 'Manager' (building the system that writes the code).
2. The Pain of Delegation: Relinquishing control over the product you created is physically painful for a founder, but absolutely necessary for the company to scale.
parts.audio: If you are the smartest person in the room, your company will never grow larger than your own brain. The job of a mature CEO is to hire people who are vastly superior at coding, sales, and marketing, and then get out of their way.

questions.question: A CEO hires a brilliant VP of Marketing, but the CEO constantly changes the colors on the website and rewrites the ad copy. What will happen?
options: The VP of Marketing will quit. High-performing executives do not tolerate micromanagement. If you hire a great leader, you must give them the autonomy to execute their vision, even if you disagree with the button colors.
questions.correct_answer: The VP of Marketing will quit. High-performing executives do not tolerate micromanagement. If you hire a great leader, you must give them the autonomy to execute their vision, even if you disagree with the button colors.
questions.explanation: Never hire a dog and then bark yourself.

questions.question: Listen to the executive coach explaining the '80% Rule'. What is the philosophy of delegation?
questions.tts_text: If someone on your team can do a task 80% as well as you can, you must delegate it to them immediately. The time you save is worth infinitely more to the company than the 20% drop in perfection.
options: Good Enough is Perfect. Startups scale on speed, not perfection. If the founder insists on doing everything 100% perfectly themselves, the company will grind to a halt. Accept the 80% and focus on strategy.
questions.correct_answer: Good Enough is Perfect. Startups scale on speed, not perfection. If the founder insists on doing everything 100% perfectly themselves, the company will grind to a halt. Accept the 80% and focus on strategy.
questions.explanation: Perfectionism is a disease that kills scale.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'Delegation' and 'Abdication'?
options: Delegation is giving someone a task but maintaining a system to verify the results. Abdication is blindly throwing a task over the wall, ignoring it completely, and acting surprised when it fails. Trust, but verify.
questions.correct_answer: Delegation is giving someone a task but maintaining a system to verify the results. Abdication is blindly throwing a task over the wall, ignoring it completely, and acting surprised when it fails. Trust, but verify.
questions.explanation: You can delegate authority, but you cannot delegate responsibility.

questions.question: Why do many early-stage startup employees fail when the company reaches 100 people?
options: The skills required to hack a prototype together in a garage are the exact opposite of the skills required to manage a 50-person department. Many early employees cannot survive the transition from 'Hacker' to 'Executive'.
questions.correct_answer: The skills required to hack a prototype together in a garage are the exact opposite of the skills required to manage a 50-person department. Many early employees cannot survive the transition from 'Hacker' to 'Executive'.
questions.explanation: What got you here won't get you there.

pairs.match: Assigning responsibility for a task to a subordinate while maintaining accountability
Abandoning a responsibility completely without oversight
Controlling every small detail of an employee's work, destroying autonomy
A person (usually the founder) whose insistence on approval slows down the whole company
